g.text: Sample RAM organization — banks, lanes and slots
SLOT_SAMPLES = 1024 SLOT_COUNT = 4 ROWS = 128 One IQ16 sample = 32 bits
Each vertical column is a separate RAM lane. Each horizontal band is one slot's address region.

div.div:
What each term means
BANK = one channel's complete sample memory.
There are 4 banks: A, B, C and D.
LANE = one independent 512 × 32-bit RAM array.
There are 8 lanes per bank, 32 lanes total.
SLOT = one 128-row address region in every lane.
It groups the same acquisition interval across
all four channel banks.

div.div:
Capacity of one slot
In one lane:
128 rows × 4 bytes = 512 bytes
Across one bank:
8 lanes × 128 samples = 1024 IQ samples
= 4 KiB per channel
Across all four banks:
4 × 4 KiB = 16 KiB
All four slots together: 64 KiB

g.text: A slot is not a separate RAM instance: it is an address region shared by the lane RAMs.
Example: wr_slot = 2 selects addresses 256–383. wr_offset chooses the lane and row within that slot.
